intro: This branch studies polynomial functions (expressions built from powers of x, like x cubed minus 4x) as graphs. Learners find where the graphs cross zero, what shape they take, and how to find every solution of a polynomial equation.

IV.10.01.what: Finding the degree (highest power of x) and the leading coefficient (the number in front of that power) of a polynomial.

levels.a: Finds the highest power of x in a polynomial.
levels.b: Finds the number in front of that highest power.
levels.c: Finds both from a polynomial written as brackets multiplied together.
levels.d: Uses the degree to state the most zeros the graph can have.
levels.e: Finds both when brackets are raised to powers.
levels.f: Finds both when the biggest terms cancel out on subtraction.

IV.10.02.what: Predicting which way a polynomial graph heads at its far ends, from its highest power and the sign in front.

levels.a: Knows that an even highest power sends both ends the same way.
levels.b: Knows that an odd highest power sends the ends opposite ways.
levels.c: Uses the sign of the leading number to decide up or down.
levels.d: Matches graphs with the same end behavior.

IV.10.03.what: Finding the zeros of a polynomial and their multiplicity: how many times each zero is repeated.

levels.a: Reads the zeros from brackets multiplied together.
levels.b: Counts how many times a zero repeats from the power on its bracket.
levels.c: Checks the total degree by adding up the repeats.
levels.d: Matches a graph to a possible equation using its zeros.

IV.10.04.what: Predicting how a polynomial graph behaves at each zero: crossing straight through, bouncing back, or flattening as it crosses.

levels.a: Knows a graph crosses the axis at a zero that appears an odd number of times.
levels.b: Knows a graph touches and bounces back at a zero that appears an even number of times.
levels.c: Knows a graph flattens as it crosses at a zero that appears three times.
levels.d: Predicts the overall shape and picks the matching graph.
levels.e: Factors first to find how the graph behaves at each zero.
levels.f: Works out the zeros of a new graph built by putting x squared into an old one.

IV.10.05.what: Sketching a polynomial graph from its factored form, using zeros, the y-intercept and the ends.

levels.a: Marks where the graph meets the x-axis.
levels.b: Finds where the graph crosses the y-axis.
levels.c: Works out which way each end of the graph heads.
levels.d: Joins the pieces into a correct sketch.

IV.10.06.what: Finding turning points: where a graph changes from going up to going down, or the other way.

levels.a: States the most turning points possible: one less than the degree.
levels.b: Uses a graphing tool to locate turning points.
levels.c: Finds the local highest and lowest values.
levels.d: Explains a turning point in context, such as the top of a roller-coaster hill.
levels.e: Finds turning points without technology by treating x squared as one quantity.
levels.f: Finds when a graph has exactly one turning point instead of three.

IV.10.07.what: The remainder theorem: the remainder after dividing by x minus a equals the value of the polynomial at a.

levels.a: Finds a remainder by putting a number into the polynomial.
levels.b: Uses synthetic division, a quick shorthand, to divide and find the remainder.
levels.c: Uses synthetic division as a quick way to evaluate.
levels.d: Finds a missing number from a given remainder.

IV.10.08.what: The factor theorem: if a polynomial gives zero at a, then x minus a is one of its factors.

levels.a: Uses a zero output to name a factor.
levels.b: Tests whether a bracket is a factor by evaluating.
levels.c: Divides out a known factor to find what is left.

IV.10.09.what: The rational root theorem: a short list of fractions that are the only possible neat roots of a polynomial.

levels.a: Lists the candidate fraction roots from the first and last numbers.
levels.b: Tests the candidates to find every root that works.
levels.c: Finds a first root of a harder cubic.
levels.d: Divides out that root to leave a simpler quadratic.
levels.e: Clears fractions in the equation first, then finds the roots.
levels.f: Finds all whole-number values of an unknown that allow a neat root.

IV.10.10.what: Finding every zero of a polynomial, including irrational and complex ones, by combining earlier tools.

levels.b: Divides one out and solves the quadratic that is left.
levels.c: Finds irrational and complex zeros as well.
levels.e: Uses a given root's matching partner (its conjugate) to find the rest.
levels.f: Solves a symmetric fourth-power equation with a clever substitution.

IV.10.11.what: Building a polynomial when its zeros are given, working backwards from answers to equation.

levels.a: Turns each zero into a bracket and multiplies them.
levels.b: Includes repeated zeros the right number of times.
levels.c: Adds the matching partner of an irrational or complex zero.
levels.d: Scales the polynomial so it passes through a given point.
levels.e: Reads zeros and a point from a graph to write its equation.
levels.f: Finds a polynomial from three of its values using a clever subtraction.

IV.10.12.what: Solving polynomial inequalities: finding where a polynomial is above or below zero.

levels.a: Finds the zeros, where the sign may change.
levels.b: Tests the sign in each region between zeros.
levels.c: Reads the answer from a graph.
levels.d: Writes the answer as ranges in bracket form.

IV.10.13.what: Using polynomials to model real situations, such as the volume of a box folded from a sheet of card.

levels.a: Works out a box's volume for a given corner cut.
levels.b: Uses a calculator to fit a cubic to data.
levels.c: Uses a graphing tool to find the cut giving the biggest box.
levels.d: Decides which cut sizes are physically possible.

IV.10.14.what: Connecting a polynomial's roots to its numbers: for example, the roots of a quadratic add to a known value.

levels.a: Finds the sum and product of a quadratic's roots without solving.
levels.b: Builds a quadratic from the sum and product of its roots.
levels.c: Uses the matching rules for the three roots of a cubic.
levels.d: Writes a new equation whose roots are changed versions of old ones.
levels.e: Finds symmetric expressions, like the sum of the roots cubed, without solving.
levels.f: Finds a missing number when one root is a multiple of the other.
